summary: Authors may use generative AI and AI-assisted tools if they disclose the specific tools and uses and keep human oversight, taking full responsibility for the content. Disclosure goes in the methodology for research design/analysis, or in a dedicated declaration before the references for other uses; basic spelling/grammar checkers and reference managers need no disclosure. AI cannot be listed as an author, and AI creation or alteration of images is prohibited unless it is part of the research design or methods. This authors-only policy does not set rules for reviewers or editors' use of AI.

evidence.quote: authors may use generative AI and AI-assisted tools to assist with the generation of scholarly work
as long as they disclose the specific use(s) of the tool and the tool(s) used
use of spelling and grammar checking tools and reference manager tools, which may rely on AI or AI-assisted technologies does not require disclosure
Authors should not list AI or AI-assisted tools as an author or co-author
We do not permit the use of AI or AI-assisted tools to create or alter images in submitted manuscripts.
